name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090
memory_bandwidth_basis: GDDR6X 19.5 Gbps data rate x 384-bit / 8 = 936 GB/s (NVIDIA GB202/GB203 comparison table in the RTX Blackwell whitepaper prints 'Memory Clock (Data Rate) 19.5 Gbps' and 'Memory Bandwidth 936 GB/sec' for the 3090 column; the 3090 Ti column in the same table is 21 Gbps / 1008 GB/sec)
notes:
Consumer card, Ampere GA102, Samsung 8N, 10496 CUDA cores, 350 W TGP.

Bandwidth: recorded as 936 GB/s (19.5 Gbps part). Note that the RTX 3090 Ti in the SAME NVIDIA whitepaper table is 21 Gbps / 1008 GB/sec. The two 24 GB cards are not interchangeable on bandwidth; recommendations that quote '24 GB RTX 3090' from a Ti benchmark silently overstate this card.

Tensor precision: FP16 tensor with FP32 accumulate is 71.2 TFLOPS dense (the Ada whitepaper's GA102 column shows 'Peak FP16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP16 Accumulate 142.3/284.6', i.e. double with FP16 accumulate, and half again in sparse). LLM inference kernels normally accumulate in FP32, so 71.2 is the practically relevant figure. FP8/INT8/INT4 tensor throughput for GA102 was NOT verified against a primary document in this pass and is deliberately omitted rather than estimated.

For LLM inference: 24 GB is a hard ceiling on resident weights. Compare against Apple unified-memory parts on both capacity AND addressability - see the Apple records, where a 128 GB unified pool is not 5x a 24 GB VRAM pool.
